messages:
maya: Hey team — quick question on keys. I set up my account but I'm confused about which key to use for local dev vs CI. Also getting occasional 429s when streaming. Anyone point me to the simple rules?

dylan: Welcome Maya :tada: Use the SANDBOX key for local/dev and CI by default. Hosted keys are for production traffic only (they're billed).

maya: Where do I find the sandbox key in the Console? I only see a ‘create key’ button that looks like it makes a hosted key?

onboarding-bot: Hi Maya! To get a sandbox key: Console > Developer Settings > Sandbox Keys. If you don't see it, you might not have the sandbox role; file a request at /onboard-access or DM @dylan.

sam: Quick note on quotas: sandbox is rate limited and quota'd. Typical defaults in our org right now: 50k tokens/day, 30 req/minute, 3 concurrent streaming connections. If you exceed those you get 429s. If you need more for an integration test, ask for a temporary bump via the onboarding form.

maya: Got it — thanks. For CI, should I store the sandbox key as REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY?

dylan: We recommend REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for CI so it's clear. Example GitHub Actions usage: 

```yaml
- name: Set sandbox key
  env:
    REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY }}
- name: Run tests
  run: pytest tests/ --maxfail=1
```

sam: If you have a CI pool of IPs to whitelist (for hosted endpoints), talk to ops. Sandbox endpoints are generally unblocklisted, but some customers use network policies.

maya: About the 429s — any recommended client behavior? I'm streaming chat completions and sometimes it dies mid-stream.

ops-bot: When you see a 429 we include Retry-After header where possible. Backoff strategy we usually use: exponential backoff + jitter. For streaming specifically: on connection close with 429, attempt a resume with prefix caching if the SDK supports it, otherwise retry the entire request with backoff.

dylan: Also check you're not opening too many concurrent streams. For local experiments keep concurrency <= 2. If you're replaying large prompt sets, batch them or use non-streaming endpoints to avoid connection churn.

maya: One more — where do I request a hosted key when ready for staging?

onboarding-bot: For staging/hosted keys, complete the 'Hosted API Access' short form (link: https://console.redwood.ai/onboarding/hosted-access) and tag @infra-sre. Staging keys require a short justification and expected qps.

maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone — this already helps a lot :raised_hands:

dylan: Any time. Ping me if you need a quick walk-through or to get your sandbox quota bumped for tests.

sam: If you want to avoid 429s during long test runs, consider using our local mock server (devx/local-mock) which simulates responses but doesn't consume quota. DM me and I'll share the runbook.

maya: Will do — thanks!
